simple.meaning: גָּרֵב (Gârêb) is a Hebrew word meaning “Gareb , the name of an Israelite, also of a hill near Jerusalem.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גָּרֵב (H1619) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Samuel 23:38, with occurrences in 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּרֵב (H1619) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גָּרֵב (H1619) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גָּרֵב (Gârêb) / H1619 is traced through 2 Samuel 23:38, 1 Chronicles 11:40, Jeremiah 31:39 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1619. Gareb גָּרֵב 1. proper name, masculine (compare Palmyrene proper name, masculine גריבא Vog 141 ) one of David's heroes 2Sam 23:38 = 1Chr 11:40 . 2. proper name, of a location (compare Sabean proper name, of a location גרבם Hal No. 379, 382 ) only in גָּרֵב גִּבְעַת Jer 31:39 hill of Gareb , apparently close to Jerusalem on the southwest compare Gf; see also Hi Che. גַּרְגְּרוֺת גַּרְגַּר, see below גרר .
